title: Mental Health Basics: Understanding and Supporting Wellbeing
content:
Mental health encompasses emotional, psychological, and social wellbeing. It affects how we think, feel, act, handle stress, and relate to others. Like physical health, mental health exists on a spectrum — most people experience periods of difficulty, and this is a normal part of life.

Common mental health conditions include:

Depression is characterised by persistent low mood, loss of interest in activities once enjoyed, fatigue, sleep changes (sleeping too much or too little), appetite changes, difficulty concentrating, and in severe cases, thoughts of self-harm or suicide. It is not a character flaw or weakness but a medical condition with effective treatments.

Anxiety disorders involve excessive worry or fear that interferes with daily life. Common forms include generalised anxiety disorder (pervasive worry about many areas of life), panic disorder (recurrent panic attacks), social anxiety disorder (intense fear of social situations), and specific phobias.

Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) can develop after a traumatic event and involves intrusive memories, avoidance, negative changes in mood and thinking, and heightened alertness.

Evidence-based treatments:
Cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) is one of the most studied and effective psychological therapies for depression, anxiety, and many other conditions. It helps identify and change unhelpful thought patterns and behaviours.
Medications including antidepressants (SSRIs, SNRIs) and anti-anxiety medicines are effective for many people, often working best in combination with therapy.
Lifestyle factors — regular exercise, sufficient sleep, social connection, and limiting alcohol — all have evidence supporting their role in mental health maintenance and recovery.

Seeking help:
If you are experiencing mental health difficulties, speaking with a primary care doctor is a good first step — they can rule out physical causes, provide basic support, and refer to a specialist.
Mental health professionals include psychiatrists (physicians who can prescribe medication), psychologists, therapists, and counsellors.
If you or someone you know is in crisis or having thoughts of self-harm, please contact a crisis service immediately. In India, iCall is available at 9152987821. In the US, call or text 988 (Suicide and Crisis Lifeline).
source: Original — based on NIH National Institute of Mental Health public information (public domain) and WHO mental health resources
